docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Common questions and answers about FlavorPack.

docs.title: What is FlavorPack?
docs.text: FlavorPack is a Python packaging system that creates self-contained, single-file executables from Python applications. It bundles your code, dependencies, and resources into a Progressive Secure Package Format (PSPF) file that runs anywhere without installation.

docs.title: How does FlavorPack differ from PyInstaller or cx_Freeze?
docs.text: Feature FlavorPack PyInstaller cx_Freeze Output format Single .psp file Single exe or folder Folder with exe Cross-platform build Yes Limited Limited Package signing Built-in Ed25519 External tools External tools Compression Multiple codecs ZIP only ZIP only Lazy loading Yes No No Work environments Managed cache Temp extraction In-place Update mechanism Slot-based Full rebuild Full rebuild

docs.title: What platforms does FlavorPack support?
docs.text: FlavorPack supports: - Linux: x86_64 (amd64), ARM64 - macOS: Intel (x86_64), Apple Silicon (ARM64) - Windows: x86_64 (64-bit)

docs.title: What Python versions are supported?
docs.text: FlavorPack supports Python 3.9 and later, with best support for Python 3.11+.

docs.title: How do I install FlavorPack?
docs.text:
Bash
pip install flavor

docs.title: Do I need to install anything else?
docs.text: No, FlavorPack includes all necessary components. The launcher binaries are downloaded automatically on first use.

docs.title: Can I use FlavorPack in a virtual environment?
docs.text:
Yes, FlavorPack works perfectly in virtual environments:

Bash
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install flavor

docs.title: How do I update FlavorPack?
docs.text:
Bash
pip install --upgrade flavor

docs.title: What's the minimum configuration needed?
docs.text:
A minimal pyproject.toml:

TOML
[project]
name = "myapp"
version = "1.0.0"

[tool.flavor]
entry_point = "myapp:main"

docs.title: Can I include non-Python files?
docs.text:
Yes, use slots to include any type of file:

TOML
[[tool.flavor.slots]]
id = "data"
source = "data/"
purpose = "data-files"

[[tool.flavor.slots]]
id = "config"
source = "config.yaml"
purpose = "configuration"

docs.title: How do I exclude files from the package?
docs.text:
TOML
[tool.flavor.build]
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/test_*.py",
    "docs/",
    ".git/"
]

docs.title: Can I build packages for other platforms?
docs.text:
Yes, FlavorPack supports cross-platform builds:

Bash
# Build for specific platform
flavor pack pyproject.toml --platform linux_amd64
flavor pack pyproject.toml --platform darwin_arm64

docs.title: How do I reduce package size?
docs.text:
1. Enable compression: TOML

    [[tool.flavor.slots]]
codec = "tgz"

  2. Exclude unnecessary files: TOML

    [tool.flavor.build]
exclude = ["tests/", "docs/"]

  3. Strip binaries: Bash

    flavor pack pyproject.toml --strip

docs.title: How do I run a FlavorPack package?
docs.text:
Bash
# Linux/macOS
./myapp.psp

# Windows
myapp.psp.exe

# Or with Python
python myapp.psp

docs.title: Can I pass command-line arguments?
docs.text:
Yes, arguments are passed through to your application:

Bash
./myapp.psp --help
./myapp.psp --config production.yaml

docs.title: Where are packages extracted?
docs.text:
Packages are extracted to a cache directory: - Linux: /tmp/pspf/workenv/ - macOS: /REDACTED_TMP - Windows: %TEMP%\pspf\workenv\

You can override with FLAVOR_CACHE environment variable.

docs.title: How do I clean up extracted files?
docs.text:
Bash
# Clean packages older than 7 days
flavor workenv clean --older-than 7

# Clean all cached packages
flavor workenv clean --yes

docs.title: Can I run packages without extraction?
docs.text: Not currently. FlavorPack always extracts to a work environment, but caching makes subsequent runs very fast.

docs.title: How does package signing work?
docs.text:
FlavorPack uses Ed25519 digital signatures:

Bash
# Generate keys
flavor keygen --output private.pem

# Sign package
flavor pack pyproject.toml --private-key private.pem

# Verify signature
flavor verify myapp.psp

docs.title: Are packages encrypted?
docs.text: No, packages are signed but not encrypted. For sensitive data, encrypt files before packaging or use environment variables for secrets.

docs.title: Can I disable signature verification?
docs.text:
Yes, but it's not recommended:

Bash
FLAVOR_INSECURE=1 ./myapp.psp

docs.title: How secure are FlavorPack packages?
docs.text: FlavorPack provides: - Ed25519 digital signatures - SHA-256 checksums for all components - Isolated work environments - No dynamic code execution - Path traversal prevention

docs.title: How are dependencies handled?
docs.text: Dependencies specified in pyproject.toml are installed into a virtual environment during build and included in the package.

docs.title: Can I use packages with C extensions?
docs.text: Yes, FlavorPack supports packages with compiled extensions. Platform-specific wheels are automatically included.

docs.title: What if a dependency isn't on PyPI?
docs.text:
You can install from Git or local paths:

TOML
[project]
dependencies = [
    "requests>=2.0",
    "mypackage @ git+https://github.com/user/repo.git",
    "localpackage @ file:///path/to/package"
]

docs.title: Can I update dependencies after building?
docs.text: No, packages are immutable. To update dependencies, rebuild the package.

docs.title: Why is my package so large?
docs.text: Common causes: - Large dependencies (numpy, tensorflow, etc.) - Uncompressed slots - Including unnecessary files - Debug symbols not stripped

docs.title: Why won't my package run?
docs.text: Check: 1. Execute permissions: chmod +x myapp.psp 2. Platform compatibility: Built for correct OS/architecture 3. Python version: Matches build environment 4. Package integrity: flavor verify myapp.psp

docs.title: How do I debug package issues?
docs.text:
Bash
# Enable debug logging
FLAVOR_LOG_LEVEL=debug ./myapp.psp

# Extract and inspect
flavor extract-all myapp.psp --output debug/

# Verify package
flavor verify myapp.psp --deep

docs.title: Why do I get "Module not found" errors?
docs.text:
Ensure all dependencies are listed in pyproject.toml:

TOML
[project]
dependencies = [
    "all-your-deps",
    "including-transitive"
]

docs.title: Can I create multiple entry points?
docs.text:
Yes, define multiple scripts:

TOML
[project.scripts]
myapp = "myapp.cli:main"
myapp-admin = "myapp.admin:main"
myapp-worker = "myapp.worker:main"

docs.title: Can I use FlavorPack programmatically?
docs.text:
Yes, FlavorPack provides a Python API:

Python
from flavor.api import build_package_from_manifest

packages = build_package_from_manifest(
    manifest_path="pyproject.toml",
    output_path="dist/"
)

docs.title: Can I customize the launcher?
docs.text: You can build custom launchers from the Go or Rust source in the ingredients/ directory.

docs.title: Can I embed FlavorPack in CI/CD?
docs.text:
Yes, FlavorPack works well in CI/CD:

YAML
# GitHub Actions example
- name: Build package
  run: |
    pip install flavor
    flavor pack pyproject.toml --key-seed "${{ secrets.FLAVOR_SEED }}"

docs.title: Can I distribute packages through PyPI?
docs.text: No, PSPF packages are standalone executables, not Python packages. Distribute them through: - Direct download - GitHub releases - Package managers (apt, brew, chocolatey) - Container images

docs.title: How fast is package extraction?
docs.text: First run: 1-5 seconds depending on size Subsequent runs: <100ms (cached)

docs.title: Can I improve build performance?
docs.text:
Bash
# Use parallel builds
flavor pack pyproject.toml --parallel

# Use build cache
export FLAVOR_BUILD_CACHE=~/.cache/flavor/build

docs.title: How much disk space do packages use?
docs.text:
• Package file: 20-100MB typical
  • Extracted cache: 2-3x package size
  • Build cache: ~500MB

docs.title: What license is FlavorPack under?
docs.text: FlavorPack is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

docs.title: Can I use FlavorPack for commercial applications?
docs.text: Yes, FlavorPack can be used for commercial applications without restrictions.

docs.title: Do I need to include attribution?
docs.text: No attribution is required in your distributed packages, though it's appreciated.

docs.title: Where can I report bugs?
docs.text: Report bugs on GitHub Issues.

docs.title: Where can I ask questions?

  • Stack Overflow (tag: flavorpack)
  • Discord community

docs.text: Contact support@provide.io for commercial support options.

docs.title: Security Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common security-related issues and their solutions when working with FlavorPack packages.

docs.title: Invalid Signature Error
docs.text:
Symptom: Package fails verification with "Invalid signature" error

Solutions: 1. Verify the package hasn't been corrupted during download 2. Ensure you're using the correct public key for verification 3. Check if the package was signed with the expected key

Bash
# Verify package integrity
flavor verify myapp.psp --key-file public.key

# Check package signature details
flavor inspect myapp.psp --show-signature

docs.title: Missing Signature
docs.text:
Symptom: Package has no signature when one is expected

Solution: Re-sign the package or build with signing enabled:

Bash
# Sign an existing package
flavor sign myapp.psp --key-file private.key

# Build with signing
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --sign --key-file private.key

docs.title: Extraction Permission Denied
docs.text:
Symptom: Cannot extract package due to permission errors

Solutions: 1. Check file system permissions 2. Ensure sufficient disk space 3. Verify the extraction directory is writable

Bash
# Check permissions
ls -la ~/.cache/flavor/workenv/

# Fix permissions
chmod 755 ~/.cache/flavor/workenv/

docs.title: Execution Permission Denied
docs.text:
Symptom: Package executable cannot run

Solution: Ensure the package has execute permissions:

Bash
# Add execute permission
chmod +x myapp.psp

# Check permissions
ls -la myapp.psp

docs.title: Lost Private Key
docs.text:
Symptom: Cannot sign packages due to missing private key

Prevention: - Always backup private keys securely - Use key management systems for production - Rotate keys periodically

docs.title: Key Format Errors
docs.text:
Symptom: "Invalid key format" when signing or verifying

Solution: Ensure keys are in the correct Ed25519 format:

Bash
# Generate new key pair
flavor keygen --output keys/

# Convert existing keys if needed
flavor keys convert --input old.key --output new.key

docs.title: Development Environment
docs.text:
Bash
# Use separate keys for development
flavor keygen --output dev-keys/

# Enable insecure mode for local testing only
export FLAVOR_INSECURE=1

docs.title: Production Environment
docs.text:
1. Never share private keys
  2. Use environment variables for sensitive data
  3. Enable signature verification
  4. Audit package contents before deployment
Bash
# Audit package contents
flavor inspect myapp.psp --detailed

# Verify before running
flavor verify myapp.psp && ./myapp.psp

docs.title: Insecure Mode Warning
docs.text:
Warning: "Running in insecure mode - signatures not verified"

Solution: Remove FLAVOR_INSECURE=1 from environment for production use

docs.title: Weak Key Warning
docs.text:
Warning: "Key strength below recommended minimum"

Solution: Generate new keys with proper entropy:

Bash
# Generate strong keys
flavor keygen --output keys/ --strength high

  3. Report security vulnerabilities privately via GitHub Security Advisories

docs.text: Comprehensive troubleshooting and optimization guide for FlavorPack on Linux systems.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Linux offers excellent support for FlavorPack packages with native performance, robust security features, and broad distribution compatibility. This guide covers Linux-specific issues, optimizations, and best practices.

docs.title: Officially Tested
docs.text: Distribution Versions Architecture Notes Ubuntu 20.04, 22.04, 24.04 amd64, arm64 Primary development platform Debian 10, 11, 12 amd64, arm64 Stable, wide compatibility RHEL/CentOS 8, 9 amd64, arm64 Enterprise support Fedora 37, 38, 39 amd64, arm64 Latest features Alpine 3.16, 3.17, 3.18 amd64, arm64 Minimal, container-friendly Arch Rolling amd64, arm64 Bleeding edge

docs.title: Minimum Requirements
docs.text:
• Kernel: 3.10+ (4.19+ recommended)
  • glibc: 2.17+ (2.31+ recommended)
  • Storage: 100MB free in /tmp
  • Memory: 256MB RAM minimum

docs.title: 1. Permission Denied
docs.text:
Problem: Cannot execute package

Bash
$ ./package.psp
bash: ./package.psp: Permission denied

Solutions:

Bash
# Add execute permission
chmod +x package.psp

# Check file permissions
ls -la package.psp

# Verify filesystem allows execution
mount | grep noexec

# If on noexec filesystem, copy elsewhere
cp package.psp ~/bin/
chmod +x ~/bin/package.psp
~/bin/package.psp

docs.title: 2. Library Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: Missing shared libraries

Bash
$ ./package.psp
./package.psp: error while loading shared libraries: libssl.so.1.1: cannot open shared object file

Solutions:

Bash
# Check dependencies
ldd package.psp

# Install missing libraries
# Ubuntu/Debian
apt-get update
apt-get install libssl1.1

# RHEL/CentOS
yum install openssl-libs

# Fedora
dnf install openssl-libs

# Alpine
apk add openssl

# Use LD_LIBRARY_PATH (temporary)
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
./package.psp

docs.title: 3. SELinux Blocking Execution
docs.text:
Problem: SELinux prevents execution

Bash
$ ./package.psp
bash: ./package.psp: Permission denied
$ getenforce
Enforcing

Solutions:

Bash
# Check SELinux denials
ausearch -m avc -ts recent

# Set proper context
chcon -t bin_t package.psp

# Create custom policy
grep package.psp /var/log/audit/audit.log | audit2allow -M mypackage
semodule -i mypackage.pp

# Temporary disable (not recommended for production)
setenforce 0
./package.psp
setenforce 1

docs.title: 4. AppArmor Restrictions
docs.text:
Problem: AppArmor blocking access

Solutions:

Bash
# Check AppArmor status
aa-status

# Put in complain mode
aa-complain /path/to/package.psp

# Disable for specific binary
ln -s /etc/apparmor.d/package.psp /etc/apparmor.d/disable/
apparmor_parser -R /etc/apparmor.d/package.psp

# Create custom profile
aa-genprof package.psp

docs.title: 5. Out of Memory
docs.text:
Problem: Package killed by OOM killer

Bash
$ dmesg | grep -i "killed process"
Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (package.psp)

Solutions:

Bash
# Check memory usage
free -h
ps aux | grep package.psp

# Increase swap
dd if=/dev/zero of=/swapfile bs=1G count=4
chmod 600 /swapfile
mkswap /swapfile
swapon /swapfile

# Adjust OOM score
echo -1000 > /proc/$(pgrep package.psp)/oom_score_adj

# Use memory limits
systemd-run --scope -p MemoryLimit=2G ./package.psp

docs.title: Temporary Directory
docs.text:
Problem: No space in /tmp

Bash
$ ./package.psp
Error: No space left on device

Solutions:

Bash
# Check /tmp usage
df -h /tmp

# Clean /tmp
find /tmp -type f -atime +7 -delete

# Use different temp directory
export TMPDIR=/var/tmp
export FLAVOR_CACHE=/var/cache/flavor
./package.psp

# Mount larger /tmp
mount -o remount,size=2G /tmp

docs.title: File System Types
docs.text:
Compatibility by filesystem:

Filesystem Support Notes ext4 ✅ Excellent Default for most distros xfs ✅ Excellent Good for large files btrfs ✅ Good COW can affect performance zfs ✅ Good Compression beneficial nfs ⚠️ Limited Network latency issues cifs/smb ⚠️ Limited Permission mapping issues

docs.title: Case Sensitivity
docs.text:
Problem: Case sensitivity issues

Python
# Fix in Python code
from pathlib import Path

def find_file_case_insensitive(directory, filename):
    """Find file ignoring case."""
    directory = Path(directory)
    for file in directory.iterdir():
        if file.name.lower() == filename.lower():
            return file
    return None

docs.title: Firewall Configuration
docs.text:
Problem: Network connections blocked

Bash
# Check firewall status
# iptables
iptables -L -n

# firewalld
firewall-cmd --list-all

# ufw
ufw status verbose

Solutions:

Bash
# iptables - allow outbound
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT

# firewalld - add service
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=https
firewall-cmd --reload

# ufw - allow application
ufw allow out 443/tcp

docs.title: DNS Resolution
docs.text:
Problem: Cannot resolve hostnames

Bash
# Debug DNS
nslookup example.com
dig example.com
cat /etc/resolv.conf

Solutions:

Bash
# Add DNS servers
echo "nameserver 8.8.8.8" >> /etc/resolv.conf
echo "nameserver 1.1.1.1" >> /etc/resolv.conf

# Use systemd-resolved
systemctl restart systemd-resolved

# Configure NetworkManager
nmcli connection modify eth0 ipv4.dns "8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1"

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Docker
# Optimal Dockerfile for FlavorPack
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Install minimal dependencies
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Copy package
COPY package.psp /app/package.psp
RUN chmod +x /app/package.psp

# Create non-root user
RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash appuser
USER appuser

# Set environment
ENV FLAVOR_CACHE=/tmp/flavor

# Run
CMD ["/app/package.psp"]

docs.title: Kubernetes

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: flavorpack-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: myapp:latest
    command: ["/app/package.psp"]
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: "1Gi"
        cpu: "1"
      requests:
        memory: "256Mi"
        cpu: "250m"
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tmp
      mountPath: /tmp
    - name: cache
      mountPath: /cache
    env:
    - name: FLAVOR_CACHE
      value: /cache
  volumes:
  - name: tmp
    emptyDir: {}
  - name: cache
    emptyDir: {}

docs.title: Systemd Service
docs.text:
INI
# /etc/systemd/system/myapp.service
[Unit]
Description=My FlavorPack Application

[Service]
Type=simple
User=appuser

docs.title: macOS Troubleshooting
docs.text: Platform-specific issues and solutions for macOS users.

docs.title: Unverified Developer Warning
docs.text:
Symptom: "Cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified"

Solution: Bash

# Remove quarantine attribute
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine myapp.psp

# Or allow in System Preferences
# System Preferences > Security & Privacy > General > "Allow anyway"

docs.title: Gatekeeper Blocking Execution
docs.text:
Symptom: macOS Gatekeeper prevents package execution

Solutions: 1. Sign your packages with an Apple Developer ID 2. Notarize packages for distribution 3. For development, bypass temporarily:

Bash
# Bypass Gatekeeper for testing (development only)
sudo spctl --master-disable
# Remember to re-enable: sudo spctl --master-enable

docs.title: Permission Denied on Silicon Macs
docs.text:
Symptom: Permission denied errors on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3)

Solution: Bash

# Ensure correct architecture
file myapp.psp  # Should show "arm64"

# Fix permissions
chmod +x myapp.psp

# Clear extended attributes
xattr -c myapp.psp

docs.title: Wrong Architecture Binary
docs.text:
Symptom: "Bad CPU type in executable"

Solution: Build for the correct architecture: Bash

# Check your architecture
uname -m  # Returns "arm64" or "x86_64"

# Build for specific architecture
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --platform darwin_arm64
# or
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --platform darwin_x86_64

docs.title: Rosetta 2 Compatibility
docs.text:
Symptom: x86_64 packages on Apple Silicon

Solution: Bash

# Install Rosetta 2 if needed
softwareupdate --install-rosetta

# Run with Rosetta explicitly
arch -x86_64 ./myapp.psp

docs.title: Command Not Found
docs.text:
Symptom: flavor: command not found

Solution: Add to PATH: Bash

# Add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bash_profile
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Reload shell configuration
source ~/.zshrc

docs.title: Python Version Conflicts
docs.text:
Symptom: Wrong Python version being used

Solution: Bash

# Use specific Python version
python3.11 -m flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml

# Or set up pyenv
brew install pyenv
pyenv install 3.11.0
pyenv local 3.11.0

docs.title: Conflicting Installations
docs.text:
Symptom: Multiple Python installations causing conflicts

Solution: Bash

# Check installations
brew list | grep python
which -a python3

# Use virtual environment
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Firewall Blocking Package Downloads
docs.text:
Symptom: Cannot download dependencies during packaging

Solution: 1. Check firewall settings 2. Allow Terminal/IDE in firewall 3. Use proxy if required:

Bash
export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.example.com:8080
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.example.com:8080

docs.title: Corrupted Cache
docs.text:
Symptom: Package fails to extract or run

Solution: Bash

# Clear FlavorPack cache
rm -rf ~/.cache/flavor/workenv/

# Clear pip cache if packaging issues
pip cache purge

# Rebuild package
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --force

docs.title: Using macOS Keychain
docs.text:
Store signing keys securely: Bash

# Add key to keychain
security add-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "flavorpack-key" -w

# Use in scripts
KEY=$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER" -s "flavorpack-key" -w)

docs.title: App Bundle Creation
docs.text:
Convert to macOS app bundle: Bash

# Create app structure
mkdir -p MyApp.app/Contents/MacOS
cp myapp.psp MyApp.app/Contents/MacOS/

# Add Info.plist
cat > MyApp.app/Contents/Info.plist << EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" 
  "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>CFBundleExecutable</key>
    <string>myapp.psp</string>
    <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key>
    <string>com.example.myapp</string>
    <key>CFBundleName</key>
    <string>MyApp</string>
    <key>CFBundleVersion</key>
    <string>1.0.0</string>
</dict>
</plist>
EOF

Bash
# Check system version
sw_vers

uname -m

# Check code signing
codesign -dv myapp.psp

# Check dependencies
otool -L myapp.psp

export FLAVOR_LOG_LEVEL=debug

sudo dtruss ./myapp.psp 2>&1 | head -100

docs.title: Windows Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Platform-specific issues and solutions for Windows users.

Beta Support

Windows support is currently in beta. Some features may be limited or require additional configuration.

docs.title: Windows Defender SmartScreen
docs.text:
Symptom: "Windows protected your PC" warning

Solution: 1. Click "More info" on the warning dialog 2. Click "Run anyway" 3. Or permanently allow:

PowerShell
# Add to Windows Defender exclusions (as Administrator)
Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "C:\Path\To\myapp.psp"

# Or disable SmartScreen for the file
Unblock-File -Path .\myapp.psp

docs.title: Execution Policy Restrictions
docs.text:
Symptom: Scripts blocked by execution policy

Solution: PowerShell

# Check current policy
Get-ExecutionPolicy

# Set for current user (temporary)
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process

# Set for current user (permanent)
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser

docs.title: Access Denied Errors
docs.text:
Symptom: Cannot execute or access package

Solution: PowerShell

# Run as Administrator
Start-Process myapp.psp -Verb RunAs

# Check file permissions
Get-Acl .\myapp.psp | Format-List

# Grant execute permission
$acl = Get-Acl .\myapp.psp
$permission = "Everyone","ReadAndExecute","Allow"
$accessRule = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule $permission
$acl.SetAccessRule($accessRule)
Set-Acl .\myapp.psp $acl

docs.title: UAC (User Account Control)
docs.text:
Symptom: UAC prompts or blocks execution

Solution: PowerShell

# Create scheduled task to bypass UAC
$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "C:\Path\To\myapp.psp"
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date)
$principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "$env:USERNAME" -RunLevel Highest
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "MyApp" -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Principal $principal

docs.title: Command Not Found
docs.text:
Symptom: flavor not recognized as command

Solution: PowerShell

# Add to PATH (current session)
$env:Path += ";C:\Path\To\FlavorPack"

# Add to PATH (permanent)
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(
    "Path",
    $env:Path + ";C:\Path\To\FlavorPack",
    [EnvironmentVariableTarget]::User
)

# Verify PATH
$env:Path -split ';' | Select-String flavor

docs.title: Python Version Issues
docs.text:
Symptom: Wrong Python version or not found

Solution: PowerShell

# Check Python versions
py -0

# Use specific version
py -3.11 -m flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml

# Set default version
py -3.11 -m pip install --upgrade pip

docs.title: Real-time Protection Blocking
docs.text:
Symptom: Package quarantined or deleted

Solution: PowerShell

# Windows Defender exclusions
Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "C:\FlavorPack"
Add-MpPreference -ExclusionProcess "myapp.psp"

# Check quarantine
Get-MpThreatDetection

# Restore from quarantine
Restore-MpThreatDetection -ThreatID <ID>

docs.title: Long Path Support
docs.text:
Symptom: Path too long errors

Solution: PowerShell

# Enable long paths (requires restart)
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem" `
    -Name "LongPathsEnabled" -Value 1 -PropertyType DWORD -Force

# Or use Group Policy:
# Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Filesystem
# Enable "Enable Win32 long paths"

docs.title: NTFS Permissions
docs.text:
Symptom: Permission inheritance issues

Solution: PowerShell

# Reset permissions
icacls .\myapp.psp /reset

# Grant full control
icacls .\myapp.psp /grant "$env:USERNAME:(F)"

# Remove inheritance
icacls .\myapp.psp /inheritance:r

docs.title: Windows Firewall
docs.text:
Symptom: Network connections blocked

Solution: PowerShell

# Allow through firewall
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "FlavorPack" `
    -Direction Outbound -Program "C:\Path\To\myapp.psp" `
    -Action Allow

# Check firewall rules
Get-NetFirewallRule | Where-Object {$_.DisplayName -like "*flavor*"}

# Disable firewall temporarily (not recommended)
Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain,Public,Private -Enabled False

docs.title: Proxy Configuration
docs.text:
Symptom: Cannot download dependencies

Solution: PowerShell

# Set proxy
$env:HTTP_PROXY = "http://proxy.company.com:8080"
$env:HTTPS_PROXY = "http://proxy.company.com:8080"

# Set system proxy
netsh winhttp set proxy proxy.company.com:8080

# Check proxy settings
netsh winhttp show proxy

docs.title: Creating Windows Service
docs.text:
PowerShell
# Install as service using NSSM
nssm install MyApp "C:\Path\To\myapp.psp"
nssm set MyApp AppDirectory "C:\Path\To"
nssm set MyApp DisplayName "My FlavorPack App"
nssm set MyApp Description "FlavorPack application service"
nssm start MyApp

# Or using sc.exe
sc create MyApp binPath= "C:\Path\To\myapp.psp" DisplayName= "My FlavorPack App"
sc start MyApp

docs.title: Creating Desktop Shortcut
docs.text:
PowerShell
# Create shortcut
$WshShell = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell
$Shortcut = $WshShell.CreateShortcut("$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\MyApp.lnk")
$Shortcut.TargetPath = "C:\Path\To\myapp.psp"
$Shortcut.WorkingDirectory = "C:\Path\To"
$Shortcut.IconLocation = "C:\Path\To\icon.ico"
$Shortcut.Description = "My FlavorPack Application"
$Shortcut.Save()

docs.title: Registry Integration
docs.text:
PowerShell
# Add to context menu
$regPath = "Registry::HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\*\shell\RunWithFlavorPack"
New-Item -Path $regPath -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name "(Default)" -Value "Run with FlavorPack"
New-Item -Path "$regPath\command" -Force
New-ItemProperty -Path "$regPath\command" -Name "(Default)" `
    -Value '"C:\Path\To\myapp.psp" "%1"'

docs.text:
PowerShell

Get-EventLog -LogName Application -Newest 50 | Where-Object {$_.Message -like "*flavor*"}

docs.title: Troubleshooting Script
docs.text:
PowerShell
# diagnose-flavor.ps1 - Diagnostic script for FlavorPack on Windows

Write-Host "=== System Information ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$os = Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem
Write-Host "OS: $($os.Caption) $($os.Version)"
Write-Host "Architecture: $($os.OSArchitecture)"

Write-Host "`n=== Python Information ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
py -0
python --version

Write-Host "`n=== Package Information ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Get-Item .\myapp.psp | Format-List Name, Length, LastWriteTime, Attributes

Write-Host "`n=== Security ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Get-ExecutionPolicy
Get-MpPreference | Select-Object ExclusionPath, ExclusionProcess

Write-Host "`n=== Environment ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
$env:Path -split ';' | Select-String -Pattern "flavor|python"
Get-ChildItem Env: | Where-Object {$_.Name -like "FLAVOR*" -or $_.Name -like "PYTHON*"}

Write-Host "`n=== Network ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Test-NetConnection pypi.org -Port 443
netsh winhttp show proxy

Write-Host "`n=== Test Execution ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
& .\myapp.psp --version
